The Electrek Podcast featured this week's episode on sustainable transport and energy news, with the show airing live every Friday at 4 p.m. ET on Electrek's YouTube channel. The hosts discussed several topics in the episode, including Tesla FSD v15, Volvo XC60/90 PHEVs, Porsche Boxster EV, and additional items.

An accompanying post was published on the site with an embedded link to the live stream, where viewers were encouraged to submit questions and comments via the YouTube channel. The video is archived on YouTube after the show ends at around 5 p.m. ET, while the audio becomes available across podcast apps.

The hosts also promoted their Patreon program as a way for supporters to help reduce ads and fund additional content investment, noting that they offer gifts for Patreons with more planned.
items.title: Electrek Podcast Covers Tesla FSD v15, Volvo PHEVs, Porsche Boxster EV

items.summary:
John Thornhill of the Financial Times argues that Jensen Huang, Nvidia's founder and former boss who was reinstated after an 11-day exile, is clinging to a flawed 'great man theory' of leadership. On Monday (Nov 23), Huang's return boosted Nvidia's stock market value by almost US$1 trillion, prompting President Donald Trump to tell CNBC that the company must protect its geniuses and that Huang is certainly one.

Thornhill notes that investors have good reason for embracing this theory, which echoes historian Thomas Carlyle's view that world history is essentially the biography of great men. Three of the top 10 most valuable US public companies are still run by their founders (Nvidia, SpaceX and Meta), a figure that would rise to four if Tesla were included given Elon Musk's role since its early days; Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon remain heavily influenced by their creators even though non-founders now lead them. Tech investor Paul Graham has argued that founders possess the vision, passion, knowledge and grit that professional managers lack, warning that bringing in outside executives sometimes drove promising companies into decline.

Thornhill contends that this theory has clear limits: just as Napoleon would not have risen to power without the French Revolution four years earlier, Huang built Nvidia only through the deep learning revolution in AI. He asserts that all companies eventually outgrow their founders and must revert to manager mode, pointing to Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet as examples that may have lost their innovative spark but added enormous stock market value since handing over management. A person close to Huang reportedly told the Financial Times that he should be seeking super voting shares so he could control the board next time.

Thornhill warns this would be a mistake because Huang has made errors of judgement that will continue to trouble Nvidia, including newly empowered Democrats holding hearings on whether it knowingly evaded chip export restrictions to China and the Securities and Exchange Commission reportedly investigating its accounting practices amid suggestions from Treasury secretary Scott Bessent about 'seemingly illicit sales' to China. The S&P credit rating agency warned this week of a possible downgrade over weak board independence and key man risk, while Nvidia's share price has been sliding again; Thornhill concludes that founder mode no longer works at Nvidia and that Huang should work out how to switch to manager mode.
items.title: Commentary Argues Nvidia's Founding-Founder Model Is Failing

items.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India convened the 31st meeting of its Standing Advisory Committee on credit flow to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Kolkata on November 27, 2026. The session was chaired by RBI Deputy Governor Swaminathan J, who focused deliberations on accelerating credit sanctions and reducing collateral dependence for small businesses.

During the meeting, the Deputy Governor acknowledged MSMEs' role in India's economy and development goals while urging banks to speed up credit approvals and shift toward cash-flow-based lending through the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and other digital channels. He also called for wider adoption of the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) to support receivables financing, along with early identification and resolution of financial stress within the sector.

The committee conducted a broad review of working capital and investment credit flowing to MSMEs, examining lending patterns for first-time borrowers and evaluating the extent of credit guarantee coverage. Participants discussed the higher limit set for collateral-free lending to micro and small enterprises, settlement of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSE) invoices via TReDS, and key provisions of the MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026.

The meeting brought together senior government officials from the Ministry of MSME and the Department of Financial Services under the Ministry of Finance. Managing directors and executive directors of select banks attended alongside heads of SIDBI, NABARD, CGTMSE, NCGTC, and KVIC, as did the Chief Executive Officer of the Indian Banks' Association and representatives from national, regional, and state-level MSME associations.

The Deputy Governor invited industry associations to participate actively in outreach events, specifically pointing to RBI town halls and district-level MSME SAMVAAD meetings as platforms to raise awareness and bring member concerns directly to banks.
items.title: RBI Pushes Banks to Accelerate MSME Lending via Cash-Flow-Based Channels
